body.p: Claims 1-20 are pending in the current application. Claims 1-8 are withdrawn from consideration. Claims 9-17 and 20 are rejected on the ground of nonstatutory double patenting as being unpatentable over claims 9-17 and 20 of U.S. Patent No. 11,214,275. Claims 9-17 and 20 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being obvious over U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2017/0371507 to Cengil et al. ("Cengil") in view of U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2006/0284839 to Breed et al. ("Breed"). Claim 18 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being obvious over Cengil and Breed, and in further view of U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2014/0116178 to Sata ("Sata"). Claim 19 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being obvious over Cengil and Breed, and in further view of U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2006/0224945 to Kahn et al. ("Khan"). Reconsideration is respectfully requested in view of the remarks and amendments submitted herewith.

The title of the application has been objected to for not being descriptive. The title is hereby amended to recite "Vehicles, Systems, and Methods for Selecting a Recommended Vehicle Driving Mode" as suggested by the Examiner.

As noted hereinabove, claims 9-17 and 20 have been rejected on the ground of nonstatutory double patenting as being unpatentable over claims 9-17 and 20 of U.S. Patent No. 11,214,275. The rejections are respectfully traversed.

To expedite prosecution of the application, and without prejudice, Applicant submits a terminal disclaimer to obviate the double patenting rejections. Accordingly it is respectfully submitted that the double patenting rejections are overcome and withdrawal of the rejections is respectfully requested.
As noted hereinabove, claims 9-17 and 20 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being obvious over Cengil and Breed. Claim 18 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being obvious over
Cengil and Breed, and in further view of Sata. Claim 19 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being obvious over Cengil and Breed, and in further view of Khan.

Applicant respectfully disagrees that the combination of Cengil and Breed teaches each and every element of claims 9 and 16. Contrary to the Office's assertions, the cited references fail to teach or suggest at least "navigate the menu of the driving mode options of the vehicle using the driving mode paddle shifter" and "receive a drive mode shifting signal from the driving mode paddle shifter indicative of a selection of one or the driving mode options in the menu with the driving mode paddle shifter," as recited in independent claim 9 and as similarly recited in independent claim 16. The Office relies on Cengil for teaching these features. Office Action P. 12-13, 23-26. However, Cengil only discloses changing a background image to correspond to a recommended driving mode and allowing a user to confirm the recommended driving mode. Cengil, para. [0063]. In other words, Cengil does not disclose a user navigating or selecting between a menu of driving mode options. Rather, Cengil discloses a user merely confirming a single recommended option, or the system automatically selecting the recommended option. That is, Cengil takes the ability to select the driving mode out of the hands of a user and instead relies on the system automatically making the selection. Consequently, Cengil fails to teach or suggest at least "navigate the menu of the driving mode options of the vehicle using the driving mode paddle shifter" and "receive a drive mode shifting signal from the driving mode paddle shifter indicative of a selection of one or the driving mode options in the menu with the driving mode paddle shifter," as recited in independent claim 9 and as similarly recited in independent claim 16.

Further, the Office admits that Cengil fails to teach a paddle shifter. Office Action P. 13. Instead, the Office relies on Breed as teaching a steering wheel with a driving model paddle shifter coupled to the steering wheel. Office Action P. 14. However, Breed merely discloses only buttons, switches, rotary knobs, and scroll wheels as alleged "finger triggers." Breed, para. [1025-1038]. That is, Breed is silent with respect to paddle shifters.

Neither Sata nor Khan rectifies the deficiencies of Cengil and Breed, nor where they relied on as such. Sata was relied on for teaching additional functionality of a paddle shifter, and Khan was relied on for teaching operating the paddle shifters in a predetermined sequence to achieve various outputs. Office Action P. 29, 30.

In view thereof, Applicant submits that none of the cited references, whether viewed singly or in combination, teach the claimed features as now defined in independent claims 9 and 16. Therefore, Applicant respectfully requests that the rejection be withdrawn as independent claims 9, and 16 are believed to be allowable.

Based on the foregoing, Applicant respectfully submits that independent claims 9 and 16, and all claims that depend thereon, can no longer be rejected as being obvious in view of Cengil, Breed, Sata, or Khan, either alone or in combination. Withdrawal of the rejections and a timely notice of allowance are respectfully requested.

In view of the above remarks, Applicant respectfully submits that the application is now in condition for allowance. The Examiner is encouraged to contact the undersigned to resolve efficiently any formal matters or to discuss any aspects of the application or of this response. Otherwise, early notification of allowable subject matter is respectfully requested.

No additional fees are believed to be due. However, the Director is hereby authorized to charge all required fees (including any extension of time fees) and to credit any overpayment of fees in this and any concurrent or future correspondence to Deposit Account No. 041133.
